title: The Agent Behind the Curtain: Building the Oz Cloud Agent Platform — Safia Abdalla, Warp
talk_summary: Safia Abdalla describes Warp's Oz cloud agent platform: sandboxes, multi-harness support, agent/sub-agent orchestration, and an API exposing every primitive. The most concrete operational lesson is their open-source PR pipeline where agents triage issues, draft specs, implement, and gate reviews before any human is pinged.

takeaways.technique: Agent review gate before human reviewers
takeaways.what_they_do: All contributed PRs go through an agent-managed review process over multiple iterations; human reviewers are only pinged after an agent approves, so humans see only high-signal PRs.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we don't actually ping any of the human reviewers on our team until an agent has approved our PRs
takeaways.numbers: thousands of PRs after open-sourcing; GitHub stars 20k to 60k

takeaways.technique: Agent triage of incoming issues with clarifying questions
takeaways.what_they_do: When an issue is filed, an agent researches the codebase, asks the reporter clarifying questions if the request is vague, and drafts an initial spec before implementation.
takeaways.evidence_quote: an agent will kick in and start to triage the issue automatically. It'll do research across the codebase

takeaways.technique: Heterogeneous agents per role (research/plan, implement, validate) with different harnesses/models
takeaways.what_they_do: They split work across a planner, implementer, and validator agent, deliberately using different harnesses and models for an adversarial, robust result.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you might want each of these agents to use different harnesses and different models in order to have a real adversar adversarial and robust approach

takeaways.what_they_do: Platform abstracts where the agent runs, supporting both managed hosting and self-hosted/self-brought infrastructure behind one interface.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we add support for not only managed hosting but also self-hosting to the platform

takeaways.technique: API for every primitive, enabling non-engineers to build bots
takeaways.what_they_do: Every key component (agents, sub-agents, environments, artifacts) is exposed via API/SDK, letting non-engineering teammates build custom Slack bots and workflows.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we're trying to be intentional about exposing an API for every key component of the stack

takeaways.technique: Self-improvement loop from accumulated PR examples
takeaways.what_they_do: They improve the review/triage agents as more PRs and code examples arrive, treating the agent as something refined by observed cases.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we improve the agent as um we get more PRs in the repo and we see more examples of code
